Augustine of Hippo, *Reply to Faustus the Manichaean* 19.11 — “what was thus prefigured is fulfilled in Christ, who leads us to a new life by purging out the leaven of the old life”
John Chrysostom, *Homilies on First and Second Corinthians* 15.35 — “since of course the punishment being so great in that which is a shadow, in our case it cannot choose but be much greater.”

label: The unmuzzled ox treading the grain → the preachers of the gospel
def: The Law: rites, feasts, sacrifices. Seen by 2 Fathers: Anonymous Early Writings, Tertullian.
where: Tertullian, *The Five Books Against Marcion* 5.20 — “Thus he showed that the law had a symbolic reference to ourselves”

Anonymous Early Writings, *Constitutions of the Holy Apostles* 7.3 — “As, therefore, the ox that labours in the threshing-floor without a muzzle eats indeed, but does not eat all up; so do you who labour in the threshing-floor, that is, in the Church of God, eat of the Church”
